precepts.text: Sufficient to such a man is this punishment: he got punished for his action because he was in error. Now contrariwise ye ought rather to forgive him, and comfort him. Some brothers do not have the spirit to comfort; they look at the comfort part as weak. The Bible says forgive and comfort him, lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow: you never allow him to grow out of the situation, he feels repentance is hopeless, and you destroy a brother. Confirm your love toward him. It is not a weak nature to forgive a brother and confirm your love: I see you fighting, you are trying to get right, we are here for you. And do it lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices, and one of his devices is unforgiveness. If a brother has not committed the same infraction again, why do you keep bringing it up over and over? That is something you are battling.
precepts.point: Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing, lacking nothing.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations.” Why count it joy? Because you are learning about yourself, what you have to fix. Some come to this truth and never knew they deal with a spirit of unforgiveness. They can’t let somebody off the hook for something that happened ten years ago, five years ago; they still harbor it. The word of God reveals it: I struggle with getting past things. Good, because now you can learn how to forgive, and you want forgiveness yourself. That is a trying of your faith, and Paul shows it in Corinthians.

“Sufficient to such a man is this punishment, which was inflicted of many.” He got punished for his action because he was in error. “So that contrariwise ye ought rather to forgive him, and comfort him.” Contrariwise, the opposite side of his punishment: he paid it, now forgive him. Some brothers don’t have the spirit to comfort; they look at the comfort part as weak. Bro, the Bible says forgive and comfort him.

“lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.” If you don’t allow him or her to grow out of the situation, they feel it is hopeless, there is no chance to repent and get right, and you destroy a brother. “Wherefore I beseech you that ye would confirm your love toward him.” It is not a weak nature to forgive a brother and confirm your love: it’s going to be all right, I see you fighting, you are trying to get right, we are here for you. Not babying him, but not holding him to something he moved on from.

“For to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether ye be obedient in all things.” He served his punishment; now let’s see the proof of you: can you forgive? “Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” One of his devices is unforgiveness. A brother who stole may not be let into your house again; that is not what this is about. But if he hasn’t committed the same infraction again, and you keep saying remember that time you stole, five years later, that is something you are battling within you, and Satan has you. Let patience have her perfect work, “that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.”

precepts.text: Lest Satan should get an advantage of us, for we are not ignorant of his devices. Every Passover the same thing happens and people who have seen it before still fall for it. Not studying, not praying, not getting your four chapters: Satan has you where he wants you.
precepts.point: The kingdom is like leaven a woman hid in three measures of meal till the whole was leavened. Leaven grows.
precepts.why:
“Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” Every year the Passover comes around and we see the same thing happen: people start bugging out. And people who have been with us, who saw it happen before, still fall for it. We have to fight. Don't play into Satan's devices.

He wants you right where he's got you. Some are on their way out because they're not paying attention to class, not studying, not praying, not getting their four chapters, not doing anything right. Satan has you right where he wants you.

We should not be ignorant of his devices, but some remain ignorant, and the reason is that they despise wisdom and don't want to be taught. That is how the leaven gets in and spreads.

precepts.text: I have kept the ways of the Lord and not wickedly departed from my God; I did not put away his statutes from me. When Nathan confronted David over Bathsheba and Uriah, he did not answer 'I am king'; he acknowledged his sin, accepted the judgment and walked on, a man after God's heart.
precepts.point: Forgive, lest Satan should get an advantage of us, for we are not ignorant of his devices. Examine whether a subtle pride is his device on you: not asking for help, thinking too highly of yourself, refusing correction. Captain Matthew adds that pride is also why a heavy brother will not change his eating.
precepts.why:
Paul forgives “Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” So examine yourself: has Satan been using some form of pride to hold you back and keep you down? It may be subtle: not asking for help, thinking too highly of yourself, I'm good, I'm fine. Satan has many devices and can transform himself into an angel of light. Captain Matthew put it plainly: fat brothers are too prideful, and that is why they won't change their eating habits.

David shows the other way. “The Lord rewarded me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me. For I have kept the ways of the Lord, and have not wickedly departed from my God. For all his judgments were before me, and I did not put away his statutes from me.” We all know David committed adultery and put out a hit on a brother. So what does it mean that he did not put away his statutes?

When Nathan the prophet brought it to him, he said, that's me. God was going to take away the child; he fasted and prayed, and when it happened he washed his face, ate bread and said it was the Lord's judgment. He was not prideful. He did not say, I'm the king, I can have as many women as I want, God chose me. He acknowledged his sin, humbled himself and did not put the judgments away.

“I was also upright before him, and I kept myself from mine iniquity.” He went on forward and walked in the ways of the Lord, to the point where God said David is a man after my own heart, because he humbled himself when his sins were brought to him. That is how you keep Satan from getting an advantage of you.

precepts.text: A man's pride shall bring him low, but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.
precepts.point: Forgive, lest Satan should get an advantage of us, for we are not ignorant of his devices. Examine whether a subtle pride is his device on you: not asking for help, thinking too highly of yourself, refusing correction. Captain Matthew adds that pride is also why a heavy brother will not change his eating.
precepts.why:
Look what pride does: “A man’s pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.” Pride is one of Satan's devices, and it does not have to be loud and in your face. It can be subtle. Sometimes it shuts you down, I can do this on my own, I don't need anybody, and it always points the finger at somebody else and never at yourself. Pride destroyed us in the kingdom, and it can keep destroying us right now.

Pride destroyed every kingdom on the earth. The king of Assyria sent his messenger with big words against Hezekiah and the Lord, and the angel of the Lord smote a hundred fourscore and five thousand in one night; then his own sons killed Sennacherib with the sword while he worshipped his god. Nebuchadnezzar said, is not this great Babylon, built by the might of my power, and while the word was in his mouth the kingdom departed from him, and he ate grass as oxen until he knew that the Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men. Antiochus spoke proudly and was smitten with a remedyless pain of the bowels. Herod took the glory of a god and was eaten of worms.

No kingdom is exempt, not Assyria, Babylon, Greece, Rome or America. And none is more prideful than Edom, the white man, of whom it is written, the pride of thine heart hath deceived thee.

But honour upholds the humble in spirit. Nebuchadnezzar humbled himself and came back saying there is no God like the God of Daniel. David humbled himself and God called him a man after his own heart. The only way our kingdom will last forever is to walk in wisdom and humility towards God; outside of that, pride brings us low like every nation before us.

For to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether ye be obedient in all things. So Paul says, I want to know, church of Corinth, if you are actually obedient in all things.

To whom ye forgive any thing, I forgive also: for if I forgave any thing, to whom I forgave it, for your sakes forgave I it in the person of Christ. Paul says, just to give an example of what a leader will do: if you all agree, the church of Corinth, to forgive this brother, I, being over the church, being the chief apostle, forgive him as well. I do not have to know every intricacy. You forgive him? Okay, let us move on.

We just read the commandment in Leviticus 19 about not bearing a grudge. So a grudge is the opposite of forgiveness. And now we just read that unforgiveness, bearing a grudge, is a device of Satan. So bearing that grudge, something else happens, the grudge gets bigger. Something else happens, the grudge gets greater. Now you have full-blown hatred, which was the top part of the commandment we read in Leviticus 19. Do you see how perfectly that works? Satan is going to want you to do the opposite of what God has required you to do. And we cannot be ignorant of Satan's devices either.

Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices. You cannot be ignorant of the things Satan uses to get an advantage over us. What are some of them? Movies. Social media. Everything in this society, and the devices are literal too: these phones. His job is to deceive you to commit sin. Once you understand his devices, you are already ahead in the game. If you are watching a movie and a sex scene comes on, do not sit there with the popcorn taking it in; you are being deceived, and you will go home and that thought will come to your mind to go back to the porn.
For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish: to the one we are the savour of death unto death, and to the other the savour of life unto life.
